name: MONAD · 30-minute chain showcase
description: One visit, three links: QR truth to the API, paced UDP to the collector on monad03, session upload with a clock fit. No access point required — none is currently broadcasting, so the lab console's collector override decides the destination and the instrument runs on the current network.

config.description: A chain test, not a measurement. Nothing here is a result: the point is to prove that a scan reaches the API, that the phone's paced stream reaches the collector on monad03, and that the session uploads with a usable clock fit. Every later claim rests on those three links, and none of them has yet carried real data end to end.
Stamps a wallclock and a monotonic timestamp at a known position. Two sync samples are the minimum the clock gate G4 accepts, so this scan and the closing one are not ceremony.
Leave the marked zone entirely. 175 s — the same sub-block length the session uses, so this take is comparable with next week's rather than a one-off.
One person, seated, still, phone in a pocket. The still crowd is the condition that has never been measured on this hardware.
Same person, walking the zone at an ordinary pace. Seated-versus-walking at a fixed count is the cleanest contrast available in one visit.
Second clock sample. With fewer than two the fold is flagged and the session is unusable for any joint analysis — the status screen says so before you leave the room.
Session uploads, then check three things: delivered rate at the collector, the clock gate on the status screen, and the tally at /admin/lab/sessions. If all three agree, the chain is real.
